findings.message: Independently re-verified the r4 hub-loop fix with a from-scratch DFS script written against the real engine (src/engine/story-engine.ts's choicesFor/choose/meetsCondition/applyEffects), not the narrative-designer's script and not re-using any prior review's tool. Exhaustive traversal from 'start' to every ending, following only choices the engine itself reports as available via choicesFor, recording the full passage-id path to each ending, flagging any path with a repeated passage id and separately flagging any cycle/infinite loop (via a loop guard on repeated (passage, items, clues, flags) state plus a generous depth bound). Result on story.r4.json: 340 complete paths, 0 paths with a repeated passage id, 0 infinite-loop/cycle detections. Ending distribution: ending-trust 64, ending-honest-ask 64, ending-call-pell 64, ending-jump-to-ghost 64, ending-rush-alone 84. This matches the narrative-designer's and literacy-specialist's reported figures exactly, from an independently written implementation. As a sanity check on the script itself, I ran the same unmodified script against story.r3.json: 940 complete paths, 624 with a repeated passage id, 12 infinite-loop detections -- this matches the previously reported r3 numbers (624/940 repeats, 12 loops) exactly, which gives confidence that r4's clean result reflects the draft, not a bug in my script.

Hand-traced the fix mechanism against src/engine/story-engine.ts's real semantics (requires.flags = must have all listed flags; requires.notFlags = must have none of them; setFlags/addItems/addClues only ever accumulate, never clear; a choice with no requires is always available). attempted-closet/attempted-ask are now set the instant a branch is entered -- via 'to-closet'/'to-ask-around' from start, or 'gather-to-closet'/'gather-to-ask' from gathering -- before any in-branch bail choice (back-to-dessa-1, no-key-no-trick, skip-to-gathering-b, thanks-back) can run. closet-report/clue-report/gathering's branch choices all gate on these entry flags rather than on have-brass-key/have-logbook-page item possession as r3 did, so a branch that is bailed early can never be re-entered and can never reopen the gathering hub loop. This closes exactly the gap review-6-qa.r3 found (bailing out of a branch before finishing it, then returning to gathering and re-entering that same branch later). Also ran a second independent script that records, for every non-ending passage across the full traversal, how many distinct targets are ever actually reached in practice (not just the declared choice count): closet-report and clue-report each reach 2 distinct targets in practice, depending on which branch is attempted first, resolving review-6-qa.r3's minor finding that one of their two choices was never practically reachable.

Confirmed all 5 endings remain reachable with no new dead ends (reports/graph.r4.json's reachableEndings lists all 5; my own traversal above reaches all 5). Confirmed the dual-item lock at threshold is intact (open-hatch-calm requires items:[brass-key] and clues:[logbook-page], unchanged from r3). Confirmed both branches' core content is unchanged from r3 (loose-panel/find-brass-key/crack-in-wall/three-knocks on the closet side; pells-shed/old-logbook/augustas-words/hand-drawn-clock on the ask-around side) and both previously-fixed minor findings remain fixed: 'storage closet' naming is consistent everywhere (start, closet-search, gathering's and threshold's lockedHints), and loose-panel's foreshadowing ('too small for any real key... a good, sharp trick would crack it open') still matches the by-force resolution at find-brass-key, with no key ever used on that particular lock. Ran `npm run check` and saw it pass in full: eslint clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean, vitest 202/202 passed across 12 files, `npm run validate:stories` reports 'All story checks passed' (8 catalog previews plus this in-review job all ok), `npm run agents:check` ok for all 9 agents, and `vite build` succeeded. A content-integrity read of the full draft text found no sexual material, violence or gore, suicide or self-harm, or references to a specific real-world religion; the 'ghost' framing is resolved as non-supernatural throughout.

Three passages still offer two textually distinct choices that both lead to the same target, so the decision has no mechanical consequence: three-knocks ('to-gathering-a-end'/'to-gathering-a-end2', both -> closet-report), hand-drawn-clock ('to-gathering-b-end'/'to-gathering-b-end2', both -> clue-report), and into-the-walls ('step-quiet'/'call-out', both -> theo-marsh with identical downstream text). Confirmed by the exhaustive traversal above: across all 340 complete paths these three passages never reach more than 1 distinct target regardless of which option is picked. This is cosmetic/atmosphere flavor rather than a structural defect, predates r3's hub-loop fix, and is distinct from the two previously-fixed minor findings (storage closet naming, loose-panel foreshadowing), which both remain fixed. Not blocking; worth a narrative polish pass on a future revision.

The four reworded 'bail out' labels (back-to-dessa-1, no-key-no-trick, skip-to-gathering-b, thanks-back) read naturally for the target age, stay well under the 18-word sentence limit, and honestly signal that leaving the branch costs its item permanently, consistent with literacy-specialist's review-7-literacy.r4 note. All four share the idiom 'for good' to mean 'permanently' -- a plus for pattern recognition on a second read, but also the same word used in 4 of the story's choice labels, which is a mild formulaic-wording note rather than a defect. Not blocking.
